study_identification_part.si4_title: Spectral normative modeling of brain structure

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Introduce Spectral Normative Modeling (SNM) to generate efficient, high‑resolution normative ranges for cortical thickness across arbitrary regions by leveraging brain eigenmodes; benchmark against conventional approaches and demonstrate clinical utility in AD via individualized deviation maps and biomarkers.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: HCP Young Adult; HCP Aging; HCP Development
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The study clearly describes using three publicly available datasets from the Human Connectome Project: HCP Young Adult (HCP-YA), HCP Aging (HCP-A), and HCP Development (HCP-D) cohorts. The dataset names are explicitly mentioned throughout the methods section.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: This study uses three publicly available healthy brain imaging datasets that were provided and curated by the Human Connectome Project (HCP); namely, HCP's Young Adult, Aging, and Development cohorts. These cohorts collectively comprised 2473 healthy individuals (54.7% female) spanning a wide age range, from 5 to 100 years old.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: SNM yields fast, high‑resolution normative charts enabling individualized cortical atrophy mapping; in AD, vertex‑wise deviations and ETVC robustly relate to cognitive impairment.
